body: The Des Moines Register, in a story republished by Yahoo News, reported that Project 1551 filed a lawsuit on Sept. 28 in Polk County court to break JCPenney's lease at Valley West Mall. Threshold Capital, which announced Sept. 29 the closing of its purchase of the 856,000-square-foot mall and its 58-acre site, is redeveloping the property through Project 1551. The developer argued it is no longer possible to operate the mall and that the lease signed in 1974 is an unreasonable obstacle to redevelopment. The store's lease was extended in July and runs through March 31, 2032.

In counterclaims filed Nov. 3, JCPenney said the mall could have a future as a shopping center. JCPenney claims Project 1551 breached its contract with the store, including by pushing out other remaining tenants and announcing plans to close and demolish the mall. It wants the court to award damages, including for past and future lost profits and diminished rental value, and to abate its rent. The company also denied that it has impeded development or requested "extortionate payments" to terminate leases.

Threshold's president said in a news release announcing the mall's sale that the group's intent is not to force JCPenney out, according to the report. Threshold has sought to demolish the building and replace it with a mixed-use area.

timeline.label: Project 1551 files suit in Polk County court to break JCPenney's lease
Threshold Capital announces the closing of its purchase of the mall
JCPenney files counterclaims seeking damages and rent abatement
